newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatist gunmen draw jail terms.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatist gunmen draw jail terms.

text.p: A Paris court ordered two Corsican separatist activists jailed on Thursday after finding them guilty of spraying the law courts in Ajaccio, western Corsica, with machine-gun fire in 1995.
Christian Jean, 48, was sentenced to four years in prison while Patrice Murati, was given a four-year term with 15 months suspended.

During their trial, the two men admitted the attack and acknowledged their membership of the banned Corsican National Liberation Front-Historic Wing, a group compared by deputy prosecutor Jacques Fourvel to the Ku Klux Klan of the 1960s.
"For the past 20 years this organisation has been destroying things, assassinating its contemporaries. But why? Does it have nothing to say, no political plans?" Fourvel asked the court.
"It is time for the separatists to start behaving like responsible people and politicians," he said.
Corsican separatists have claimed hundreds of bombings in a low-level guerrilla campaign that has spanned two decades and is aimed at obtaining greater autonomy for the from mainland France.
The two men were questioned shortly after the November 1995 attack, in which there were no injuries. Police found three rifles, a revolver and a pistol in their vehicle.
